[gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.07192) attributes SASRec weaknesses partly to overconfidence induced by negative sampling. More negatives and generalized BCE improve results; ordinary multi-negative BCE and sampled softmax also work well with sufficiently many negatives. Its evidence supports testing these simpler alternatives, not universal gBCE superiority. The paper’s uniformly sampled softmax comparison does not establish superiority over every corrected or tuned sampled-softmax implementation. Proposed ablation: unchanged SASRec architecture with one-negative BCE, K-negative BCE, K-negative gBCE, and K-negative sampled softmax. Match K and sampling across multi-negative variants; specify BCE positive/negative weighting and softmax correction/temperature. Allocate equal total GPU-seconds and tuning opportunities, counting diagnostics and failures; report updates completed because equal epochs need not mean equal cost.

[Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish that sampled ranking metrics can reverse full-catalog model ordering even in expectation. HR@10 against 99 negatives therefore measures the pinned candidate-ranking task, not full-catalog HR@10. Keep the evaluator unchanged. With 200 users/category, one hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and the four-category macro-average by 0.125 points. Calculated worst-case standard errors under independent-user sampling are approximately 3.54 points/category and 1.77 points/macro; these exclude training randomness and candidate-resampling uncertainty.

Recommended paired analysis: retain each model’s binary hit for every identical user/candidate set; bootstrap user pairs within each category, then average the four category differences, reporting a 95% interval and category results. This follows established [bootstrap evaluation practice](https://www.nist.gov/publications/computing-confidence-intervals-common-ir-measures). Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models. Repeated checkpoint/hyperparameter selection creates [validation overfitting](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html); ordinary winner intervals do not correct it. Prespecify comparisons and checkpoint rules, log all trials, limit selection, and reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched evaluation.
